newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-RFU BIDS TO MAKE PEACE WITH ENGLISH CLUBS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-RFU BIDS TO MAKE PEACE WITH ENGLISH CLUBS.

text.p: England's Rugby Football Union on Thursday proposed talks with EPRUC, the body representing senior English clubs, in an attempt to avert a threatened breakaway.
A statement issued from Twickenham said: "The RFU has made contact with EPRUC in order to start negotiations to settle the dispute."

The statement said the RFU would propose a financial agreement for the next two years and beyond and also suggest a clear partnership for the organisation of League and Cup competitions, domestically and in Europe, in terms of finance, fixtures and future competitions.
"The RFU is determined to avoid a breakaway and will help to ensure a viable future for professional club rugby while at the same time not disadvantaging the rest of the game," it said.
"The RFU wants the clubs to commit to releasing their players for representative duties to an agreed schedule. The RFU believes the game will be stronger and better staying together.
"The RFU has goodwill towards the professional clubs and wants an agreement."
At the centre of the dispute is EPRUC's insistence on a far greater say in running the competitions and also demanding an increased share of money stemming from international matches.
Donald Kerr, chairman of EPRUC, said: "We have always been amenable to talks. We approach them in an open, positive constructive frame of mind.
"I am grateful they have contact made with us. It is nearly three weeks since we last had formal contact with RFU committee members.

"There will be no preconditions. Our position is that we have asked clubs to obtain the necessary permission under their constitutions to leave the union some time after October 11, either amicably or instantly if the RFU adopt a hostile stance."
